title: Research
text:
My research integrates experimental methods with rigorous field studies to understand human decision-making in economic contexts. I believe that bridging controlled laboratory environments with real-world observations provides the most comprehensive insights into economic behavior.
By combining lab-experimental methods with large-scale field experiments, I seek to address both fundamental theoretical questions and practical policy challenges. This dual approach allows me to test economic theories with high internal validity while ensuring that findings have external validity and real-world applicability.

title: Research
text:
Current Projects



Narratives to Sustainable Agriculture: Evidence from Madagascar’s Vanilla Farmers

Funded by Volkswagen Foundation 2023-2026 With Marcela Ibanez (Göttingen) and Viviana Uruena

This project examines how narratives can influence sustainable farming practices among vanilla farmers in Madagascar. Through a series of field experiments, we test the effectiveness of different messaging strategies in promoting environmentally sustainable agricultural methods.

Completion: 40%





Substitution between Charities

With David Reinstein (Maastricht)

Evidence from several experiments on how people substitute between charities and whether multiple charitable appeals create crowding in or crowding out of charitable contributions.

Completion: 75%





Behavioral Insights into Pension Savings

With Marcela Ibanez (Göttingen) and Sebastian Schneider (MPI Bonn)

Surveys and lab-in-the-field experiments in Bogota, Colombia, exploring financial decision-making, well-being, and cognitive ability across 1200 subjects. 600 participants also completed experiments on higher-order risk preferences.

Completion: 60%

title: Gerhard Riener
text:
I am a professor of economics at the University of Southampton and research fellow in the Behavioral Economics group at the IHS, Vienna. My research focuses on experimental methods in economics, field experiments in labour, education economics and the economics of charitable giving.

Research Curriculum Vitae











Experimental Economics
Behavioral Economics
Field Experiments
Economics of Education
Public Policy Experiments
Decision Science








Review of Economic Studies (2021)
This study demonstrates how individuals systematically overweight concentrated payoffs relative to dispersed ones, leading to time-inconsistent choices and dynamically inconsistent preferences.
Read Paper





Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization (2015)
Through two field experiments in Morocco, we examine how religious norms affect charitable giving, finding significant differences in donation patterns based on Islamic principles.
Read Paper





Working Paper (2025)
Our research investigates how economic factors contribute to political polarization, with experimental evidence showing how debt-related narratives affect partisan attitudes.
View Details





Under Review (2023)
Field evidence from performance appraisals in the public sector reveals significant hidden moral costs associated with monitoring and control mechanisms.

title: Data
text:
Data Management and Sharing Policy
I am committed to open science practices and transparent research. All data from my published research is made available through appropriate repositories after a reasonable embargo period. Research data is archived according to the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable). I am currently working on making older data available.
For inquiries about accessing data from ongoing projects or unpublished research, please contact me at g.riener@soton.ac.uk.
